count_scope: Nineteen source-profile records partition two retained reviews. Thirty-three fields do not mean thirty-three accepted scenarios or requirements.

groups.basis: The actual application dispatcher obtains owned project and receipt state synchronously, completes its SQLite commits, and only then awaits remote work. The retained source review traces the relevant production callers, commit paths and owned lease returns, including the selected audio, camera, Blender, import and export boundaries. This establishes the original source lifetime obligation without asserting renderer latency, concurrent editing or runtime SQL observations.

identity_source_observations: The immutable application revision and tree are identified by retained original Git observations.
Canonical dependency primary objects corroborate the declared fixed revision and its tree.
Workspace manifests and exact lock entries preserve the dependency closure and its roles.
Studio package and lock bodies are retained with explicit unchanged-input qualification.
Earlier source-result members retain earlier revisions; no original runtime observation is retagged.
The selected native workflow declares the dependency version without claiming that version was executed.
limitations: Evidence custody is confined to the immutable application revision identified here; it is not acceptance of a later candidate or an installed product.
All new records remain unreferenced by the retained assessments. The assessed index revision, every assessment and history entry, and the existing 22 field PASS remain unchanged.
These are source-profile observations, not additional product, unit, renderer, provider, installer or audiovisual executions.
Automated technical review does not represent an independently authenticated person or a human approval.
Whole requirements and scenarios remain separately assessed. Technical readiness, product acceptance and release authorization are not granted.

Only the database transaction lifetime statement is covered. Application responsiveness, concurrent editing, correct runtime CAS, renderer execution and the separate acceptance field remain unclosed here.
The reviewed boundary distinguishes an owned operation or receipt lease from a live SQLite transaction. It does not prohibit every mutex or claim an audit of all upstream internals.
Retained service, storage and dispatcher bodies captured on the preceding revision have a complete, explicit unchanged-input qualification. No earlier runtime result is retagged.
Each documentary identity field is narrower than its scenario. Runtime, build, environment, coverage, assertions, negative behavior and failure artifacts require their own original evidence.
The upstream revision is corroborated by retained canonical primary objects. Declared tool versions and lock contents are not assertions about installed binaries or executed suites.
Historical source-result members keep their original provenance and limitations. No prior green footer or test count becomes a result on the reviewed application revision.
The retained SDK probe failure and its qualified effect boundary remain preserved; its summary counters do not prove absence of network or durable effects.

transaction_source_assertions.purpose: The application-owned Store holds its Connection privately; the dispatcher does not carry a Transaction.
Coordinator retains service/client/custody/roots, not a borrowed SQLite transaction.
Project read returns an owned Project synchronously; a Store handle is distinct from an open SQL transaction.
Receipt methods lock/call synchronously and return owned receipt data.
Recovery claim owns an IMMEDIATE transaction and commits before returning its owned receipt.
Receipt insertion owns and commits its IMMEDIATE transaction before returning.
Read transaction snapshots commit before owned latest/watermark/page results leave storage.
Scene checks and in-memory reservation precede synchronous durable dispatching receipt; only then does the bound/unbound renderer transport await run.
The remote terminal result or error is handled afterward with fresh synchronous receipt retention; no transaction is retained across remote work.
Receipt custody is an in-process reservation map, not a SQLite transaction; its lifecycle does not redefine the original DB-specific oracle.
Recovery reads an apply result inside a local lock block and returns an owned result, with no renderer await inside that block.
Both public receipt-observation methods create/commit their local Deferred snapshot before returning an owned observation.
CasBlobLease contains IDs/digest only, with no Connection, Transaction or borrowed guard.
Lease/release write their bounded retention catalogue synchronously. Retaining a lease across native execution protects CAS bytes; it does not retain a database transaction.
Current WAV bytes are copied under a local Store guard that ends before returning preparation data.
Native meter execution awaits the same receipt coordinator after synchronous preparation; source recheck follows the result.
Prepare/recheck/release are synchronous owned-return routines; the retained lease has no SQLite transaction.
Native derivation calls await only after preparation returns; release is explicit after native termination and remains separate from transaction lifetime.
Read/project/WAV lock block ends at225; native alignment dispatch goes through the coordinator at281–290.
Qualified voice application is synchronous and consumes an already completed native object; its receipt observation has a committed owned return.
Cache reader is a synchronous Vec<byte> return; it does not dispatch a renderer or hold SQL across await.
Arc pointer identity checks select the shared service; no SQL transaction begins.
Store-bound CAS read is inside a closed block of a synchronous staging function.
Production function, not a test: closed Store block copies attached source bytes before returning.
Production synchronous attached-source read retains no SQL/lock lifetime across renderer awaits.
Production synchronous Graph source capture ends the Store block before native source use.
Production synchronous static source read copies bytes and drops its Store guard before return.
Production bound_bytes performs before/after scope checks and returns copied CAS bytes from a closed block.
Production read_saved_product_source uses a closed synchronous Store block; no test-only assumption is made.
Production asset-CAS check is synchronous, drops the Store guard at3526 and returns an owned unit result.
Both direct Store hits462/500 are in the cfg(test) module and are not production renderer paths.
Direct Store hits in this file are in cfg(test), including snapshot808 and subsequent fixture assertions.
Direct Store hit226 is the cfg(test) fixture, not the production export route.
Direct Store hit402 and later direct store calls are in cfg(test) verified-source fixtures.
